fields.label: Category Window Style
fields.description: How do you wish to draw commands in the Category Window?
fields.context: text draws category names without icons; icon draws only IconSet cells; iconText draws both; auto uses icon-only when the resolved icon-plus-name text exceeds the item text rectangle width. Icon-only modes show the selected category name in the auxiliary name window. Requires the chosen icons in img/system/IconSet.png.

fields.label: Category Text Align

fields.context: Window background type: 0=normal windowskin/frame, 1=dim background, 2=transparent. This changes the named window background, not text opacity. Example 1 selects dim.

fields.label: Cursor Sounds
fields.description: SE files player can select from for cursor SE.
fields.context: Ordered choices for the corresponding menu sound. Slot 0 is the engine/default sound regardless of its label (normally "Default"); later entries are existing audio/se basenames without extension, using the database sound volume/pitch/pan. Example ["Default","Cursor1"] assumes audio/se/Cursor1 exists. Install each asset; this list neither generates nor validates audio content.

fields.label: Font Options
fields.description: Available fonts for the player to select from.
fields.context: Ordered font-family names used by the Text Font option. Slot 0 (normally "Default") delegates to Game_System mainFontFace; indices >0 return that string if present. The list does not load font files: make the font available through the game/font loading before selecting it. An out-of-range/empty entry falls back to the engine font; an unavailable but nonempty family is handed to browser font fallback. Example ["Default","Arial"], subject to font availability.

parameters.context: Options scene presentation and lists of selectable sounds/fonts. Window background values: 0=normal frame, 1=dim, 2=transparent. CategoryStyle=auto switches to an icon when resolved label width exceeds its cell. Sound/font list slot 0 delegates to the engine default; subsequent slots require assets/fonts already available. Supply decoded object values for CLI writes; nativeDefault/example native serialization is for registry inspection, not double-encoded input.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: The name of this category as seen in the Category Window.

fields.label: Icon
fields.description: Icon used for this category.
fields.context: Zero-based cell index in img/system/IconSet.png, 16 columns across each row. Example 64 selects row 4, column 0. An option-row Icon=0 suppresses its icon prefix; category icons are still part of icon/iconText/auto styles, so category 0 selects the first cell. No image file is added by this value.

fields.label: JS: Show/Hide
fields.description: Code used to determine if this category is visible.
fields.context: JavaScript function body called with this=Window_OptionsCategory and no arguments when rebuilding category commands. Return true to include the category, false to omit it. Runtime MZ globals are available after database load. Example "return true;". Do not assume a particular saved game is loaded on the title Options screen.

fields.label: Options List
fields.description: Add options to this category here.

fields.label: Symbol
fields.description: Symbol used for this option when selected.
fields.context: Use a unique case-sensitive Symbol for a functional option and its ConfigManager key; duplicate symbols share storage and native findSymbol selects the first. Avoid existing built-in keys unless deliberately configuring that same option. Empty Symbol rows are headings without persistence callbacks; dashed symbols in the shipped list are separators with no-op callbacks. Custom symbols need their own consumer if they should change game behavior.

fields.label: Icon
fields.description: Icon used for this option.
fields.context: Zero-based cell index in img/system/IconSet.png, 16 columns across each row. Example 64 selects row 4, column 0. An option-row Icon=0 suppresses its icon prefix; category icons are still part of icon/iconText/auto styles, so category 0 selects the first cell. No image file is added by this value.

fields.label: STR: Text
fields.description: Displayed text used for this option.
fields.context: Literal option label. Nonempty text other than exactly "Untitled" overrides TextJS. Empty or "Untitled" uses the TextJS result instead. DrawJS decides how to render it; shipped rows use drawTextEx and supported escape codes.

fields.label: JS: Text
fields.description: JavaScript code used to determine string used for the displayed name.
fields.context: Function body returning option label when TextStr is empty or "Untitled"; this=Window_Options, no arguments, called during list construction/refresh. Example "return TextManager.alwaysDash;". A fixed non-placeholder TextStr bypasses this callback.

fields.label: Accessibility
fields.description: Accessibility

fields.label: JS: Show/Hide
fields.description: Code used to determine if this option is visible.
fields.context: Function body called on Window_Options with no arguments during list construction/refresh. Return true to include the row, false to omit it. Example "return ConfigManager.assistMode;". This does not gate DefaultJS/SaveJS/LoadJS, which process all nonempty symbols. Guard optional globals before reading provider settings.

fields.label: JS: Enable
fields.description: Code used to determine if this option is enabled.
fields.context: Function body called on Window_Options with no arguments for an included row. Return true to permit OK/right/left callbacks; false causes those inputs to buzz. DrawJS determines the disabled appearance. Example "return true;". This does not disable storage callbacks.

fields.label: JS: Ext
fields.description: Code used to determine if this option's ext value.
fields.context: Function body called on Window_Options with no arguments when adding a shown row. Its return becomes the command ext payload, readable through currentExt() or command data. It is not passed as the first input-callback argument (that is Symbol). Return any value your custom consumer expects; shipped default returns 0. Returning a value alone has no gameplay effect.

fields.label: Functions
fields.description: Functions

fields.label: JS: Draw Option
fields.description: Code used to draw this item into the List Window.
fields.context: Function body called to draw one row with this=Window_Options, arguments[0]=Symbol, arguments[1]=index. commandName(index) returns its resolved label, itemLineRect(index) its text rectangle in pixels, and getConfigValue(symbol) the current ConfigManager value. Draw using inherited Window_Base/Window_Selectable methods. Return value is ignored; this callback must draw the value itself. The shipped default is a complete boolean OFF/ON renderer; use it with boolean input/default/load callbacks.

fields.label: JS: Process OK
fields.description: Code used when OK button is pressed while selected.
fields.context: Function body called on confirmation/OK for an enabled row, this=Window_Options, arguments[0]=Symbol, arguments[1]=index. getConfigValue/setConfigValue read/write ConfigManager; redrawItem(index) refreshes that row and playCursorSound provides feedback. Return value is ignored. The shipped body handles booleans; a numeric option needs coordinated draw/input/default/save/load bodies. A custom scene action can use prepareOptionsCoreSceneChange before leaving to preserve selection. SaveJS must assign a JSON-serializable value to config[symbol]; its return value is unused. It runs whenever ConfigManager.makeData is requested, normally by ConfigManager.save (including native Options scene termination). LoadJS must validate and assign the stored value; it runs for a present key, even if null or the wrong type. Missing keys use DefaultJS. These callbacks share the configuration storage profile across game saves; they do not save a game slot. Changing a default does not replace an existing stored key at applyData time.

parameters.context: Ordered option categories and their rows. Use a unique case-sensitive Symbol for a functional option and its ConfigManager key; duplicate symbols share storage and native findSymbol selects the first. Avoid existing built-in keys unless deliberately configuring that same option. Empty Symbol rows are headings without persistence callbacks; dashed symbols in the shipped list are separators with no-op callbacks. Custom symbols need their own consumer if they should change game behavior. TextStr wins over TextJS unless empty or exactly "Untitled". Icon is a zero-based IconSet index. Callbacks are JavaScript function bodies, compiled at boot and called later by the game; the CLI never runs them. Category ShowJS uses this=Window_OptionsCategory. Option TextJS/ShowJS/EnableJS/ExtJS use this=Window_Options during list construction, with no arguments. DrawJS and ProcessOkJS/CursorRightJS/CursorLeftJS use this=Window_Options, arguments[0]=Symbol and arguments[1]=row index. DefaultJS runs for every nonempty Symbol after database load with this=Scene_Boot, arguments[0]=undefined, arguments[1]=Symbol; it also runs from ConfigManager.applyData with this=ConfigManager, arguments[0]=the loaded config object and arguments[1]=Symbol when that config key is absent. SaveJS/LoadJS use this=ConfigManager, arguments[0]=config object and arguments[1]=Symbol. ShowJS does not gate persistence callbacks. Callback exceptions are reported as OPT_CALLBACK_FAILED, not silently ignored. SaveJS must assign a JSON-serializable value to config[symbol]; its return value is unused. It runs whenever ConfigManager.makeData is requested, normally by ConfigManager.save (including native Options scene termination). LoadJS must validate and assign the stored value; it runs for a present key, even if null or the wrong type. Missing keys use DefaultJS. These callbacks share the configuration storage profile across game saves; they do not save a game slot. Changing a default does not replace an existing stored key at applyData time. The default is decoded inspection JSON and includes empty editor section labels Accessibility/Functions/Data. Those labels are not writable fields: omit them for whole-row/array writes, or use the functional row default published by its OPT-ITEM entry. nativeDefault is the encoded registry representation, not a value to double-encode for the CLI. Edit a leaf path to preserve other callbacks, for example /Categories/0/List/1/TextStr. The full shipped callback bodies in default document each row; optional-provider rows remain conditional.

parameters.label: Master Volume Shortcut
parameters.description: Settings regarding the Master Volume Shortcut keys.

fields.label: Shortcut
fields.description: Shortcut

fields.label: Enabled?
fields.description: Enable the shortcut?
fields.context: Hold the engine control action and press pageup/pagedown to raise/lower master volume. These are mapped actions, commonly Ctrl plus PageUp/PageDown; rebinding can change physical keys. The shortcut is intercepted when a scene/input handler queries isTriggered/isRepeated for pageup/pagedown, not by a global every-frame keyboard poll. Requires Enable=true and an initialized ConfigManager.masterVolume; the intercepted action is consumed. Values are percentage points, rounded and clamped 0..100, applied through WebAudio and saved to configuration.

fields.label: Shortcut Change Value
fields.description: What is the change amount for the shortcut key?
fields.context: Hold the engine control action and press pageup/pagedown to raise/lower master volume. These are mapped actions, commonly Ctrl plus PageUp/PageDown; rebinding can change physical keys. The shortcut is intercepted when a scene/input handler queries isTriggered/isRepeated for pageup/pagedown, not by a global every-frame keyboard poll. Requires Enable=true and an initialized ConfigManager.masterVolume; the intercepted action is consumed. Values are percentage points, rounded and clamped 0..100, applied through WebAudio and saved to configuration. change is the number of percentage points per trigger/repeat, for example 5 changes 50 to 55.

optionItems.description: Section heading: \C[16]Exploration. It draws a label, accepts no value and has no persistence callbacks.
optionItems.context: Shipped row 0 in category 0 (General); these are zero-based positions and may differ after custom authoring. Consult options lists get for the effective row before editing. showJs/gates control visibility; default here is the complete decoded shipped row, not the current player value. Callbacks are JavaScript function bodies, compiled at boot and called later by the game; the CLI never runs them. Category ShowJS uses this=Window_OptionsCategory. Option TextJS/ShowJS/EnableJS/ExtJS use this=Window_Options during list construction, with no arguments. DrawJS and ProcessOkJS/CursorRightJS/CursorLeftJS use this=Window_Options, arguments[0]=Symbol and arguments[1]=row index. DefaultJS runs for every nonempty Symbol after database load with this=Scene_Boot, arguments[0]=undefined, arguments[1]=Symbol; it also runs from ConfigManager.applyData with this=ConfigManager, arguments[0]=the loaded config object and arguments[1]=Symbol when that config key is absent. SaveJS/LoadJS use this=ConfigManager, arguments[0]=config object and arguments[1]=Symbol. ShowJS does not gate persistence callbacks. Callback exceptions are reported as OPT_CALLBACK_FAILED, not silently ignored. SaveJS must assign a JSON-serializable value to config[symbol]; its return value is unused. It runs whenever ConfigManager.makeData is requested, normally by ConfigManager.save (including native Options scene termination). LoadJS must validate and assign the stored value; it runs for a present key, even if null or the wrong type. Missing keys use DefaultJS. These callbacks share the configuration storage profile across game saves; they do not save a game slot. Changing a default does not replace an existing stored key at applyData time.
